how: The invitation calls for a CLC mark without identifying who subsequently answered through placing.
One person proposes the fandom tag and previews its appearance without visible design debate.
Perceived community size explicitly conditions the initial design's scale before any reported loss or relocation.
Building is supported only through a completion claim and a separate sighting, leaving actual placement and the builders unobserved.
Coordinates and a black-border landmark locate the proposed tag while an image link previews its design.
A person who notices the visible tag offers future protection, a preliminary commitment whose execution remains unresolved.
The protection offer does not identify who changed the tag or attribute any actual damage.
The protection pledge contains no appeal to attackers, apology, or refusal to damage neighbouring work.
A black-border landmark locates the tag without establishing a negotiated boundary or deal.
Anticipating possible trashing supplies no evidence of a call to attack anyone else's work.
The proposed location contains no report of an earlier loss followed by moving.
Celebrating completion and comparing build durations treat the achieved tags as accomplishments.
The completion edit also marks the event's end and reports the tag's surviving presence.
The completion claim states no decision about carrying the effort into later canvases or community life.
A reported completed tag does not reveal whether scripts, bots, or spare accounts were used.
The surviving responder explains discovering the tag and offers protection without explicitly accepting the original build invitation.
The invitation and preview do not identify a fake, takeover, or joking call.
Choosing a small proposal because the community is small does not establish insufficient hands for the adjusted task.
The proposal and individual pledge do not reveal whether the actual builders decided leaders, votes, sanctions, or a division of work.
The proposer calls for and maps the tag, while subsequent joining and recruitment by that person remain unresolved.
Mentioning another fandom while offering personal protection does not establish an envoy acting for a room.
An individual protection pledge does not establish enacted help between rooms or representative authority.
Checking another fandom's work and noticing this tag does not establish a coalition.
The build-time comparison identifies no rival contest, taunt after a fight, or claimed victory over another room.
The comparison of construction times gives no account of a quarrel predating the canvas.
The invitation contains no host rule or objection governing canvas discussion.
Naming the represented fandom does not establish action through lore, ideology, quarrels, or colour allegiance.
The black-border location does not identify a host granting permission or ruling over guest work.
The fandom comparison does not name a prior rivalry as a reason to attack.
The location proposal and protection offer identify no agreement whose authority members dispute.
Reporting the tag on the finished canvas does not contest a cleaned copy or another account of the event.
The call precedes the surviving sighting but no speaker attributes building to having read the invitation.
Proposing the mark and calling for it share one sentence rather than an observed starter-then-call sequence.
Seeing a visible tag supports a protection offer, while causation by a thread update and subsequent repair remain unresolved.
The protection pledge supplies no observation linking upkeep to subsequent border negotiations.
A location landmark and protection pledge supply no agreement-to-restraint sequence.
The prospective protection pledge shows neither upkeep under attack nor escalation to automated placement.
Reporting completion and celebrating it share an undated edit rather than independently timed steps.
Celebration and recording the final state share one edited passage without a measured sequence or stated causal link.
The final-state report supplies no subsequent decision about carrying the effort forward.
An initially small proposal supplies no loss-and-relocation sequence caused by insufficient hands.
The proposal, coordinates, and preview appear together without observed debate being settled by an agreed template.
The surviving reply gives an independent discovery account without attributing its commitment or any silent placement to the call.
A personal protection offer establishes neither shortage under strain nor help requested from another room.
Neither the landmark nor the protection offer reports a border deal leading to exchanged help.
The invitation and protection pledge show no call turning helpers against a rival's mark.
No attack call or reasoned refusal is established by the prospective protection pledge.
The proposed location contains no reported attack answered through a truce or deal.
A build-time comparison supplies no observed attack followed by a contest in talk.
The personal protection pledge supplies no observation of attack causing coalition membership.
An invitation alone establishes neither a flood of canvas calls nor restrictions resulting from it.
The proposal and personal pledge identify no agreement followed by a dispute over who may commit the room.
